title: A class loader that defines classes from bytes

blocks.text: A class loader follows the **parent delegation model**: asked for a class, it first asks its parent, and only when the parent cannot load it does it define the class itself. A class's runtime identity is its name **plus** the loader that defined it. A `null` parent means the bootstrap loader.
Write `BytesLoader extends ClassLoader`. `new BytesLoader(parent, classes)` gets a parent (possibly `null`) and a map from binary class name to the bytes of a `.class` file.

items: `loadClass(name)` asks the parent chain first, and defines the class from the map only when no parent can load it.
One loader defines a name **once**: asking again returns the same `Class`.
Two loaders that each define the same bytes hold two different classes.
A name that no parent and no map entry knows fails with `ClassNotFoundException`.

cases.says: A loader with a null parent defines Plugin from its bytes as a new class, distinct from the test's own Plugin and from the Plugin a second loader defines, while java.lang.String still comes from the bootstrap loader.
When the parent loader also has the bytes, the child returns the parent's class instead of defining its own.
Loading the same name twice from one loader returns the same Class, without defining it again.
A name that neither the parents nor the map know fails with ClassNotFoundException.

concepts: A class's runtime identity is its name plus its defining loader, so two loaders defining the same bytes give two distinct classes, while one loader defining a name twice is a LinkageError.
A custom class loader built with a null parent has the bootstrap loader as its parent, not the application loader.
A class loader asks its parent first and defines a class itself only when no parent can load it, so core classes always come from the bootstrap loader.
